business_domains.description: This domain encompasses all functionality related to user account lifecycle management within the application. It covers user registration (creating new accounts), authentication (sign-on and sign-off processes), and profile management (editing account details). The domain maintains personal information such as name, contact details, and address. It also handles user preferences including language preference, favorite product category, and banner display options. The persistence layer manages multiple related data stores for core account information, sign-on credentials, and user profile settings. This domain has a clear bounded context around the identity and preferences of a user, and it interacts with the catalog domain to populate personalized product lists based on user preferences.

This domain manages the entire product catalog hierarchy and inventory of the pet store. It is organized around three levels of entities: Categories (top-level groupings like Fish, Dogs, Cats), Products (items belonging to a category, like specific breeds or types), and Items (the actual purchasable SKUs with specific attributes, pricing, and supplier information). The domain provides capabilities for browsing by category, viewing product details, drilling down to individual items, and full-text product search. It also manages inventory tracking, allowing the system to check whether a specific item is currently in stock. The supplier information is a supporting concern within this domain. This domain serves as the product data source for other domains, particularly Cart and Order Management, which reference items from this catalog.

This domain manages the transient shopping experience of a customer during a single session. It allows customers to build a collection of items they intend to purchase before committing to an order. Core capabilities include adding items to the cart (with stock availability checks), removing items, updating item quantities, and calculating the cart subtotal. The domain maintains a session-scoped cart state, tracking both a map (for efficient lookup by item ID) and a list (for ordered display) of cart items. Each cart item tracks the specific catalog item, quantity, in-stock status, and total price for that line. This domain acts as an intermediary between browsing the catalog and placing a formal order, and it has a natural transition point to Order Management during the checkout process.

This domain handles the complete lifecycle of customer orders from creation through fulfillment tracking. When a customer checks out, an order is initialized from the customer's account and cart data, capturing shipping and billing addresses, payment details (credit card type, number, expiry), courier selection, and the full list of ordered line items with their quantities and unit prices. The domain manages order persistence, retrieval of order history by customer, and viewing individual order details. It also handles inventory updates when orders are placed, decrementing available stock quantities. A sequence generation mechanism is used to assign unique order identifiers. Order status tracking is maintained per line item. The domain enforces authorization rules ensuring customers can only view their own orders.
